summary: iteration_16 Linear-aesthetic dark theme visual regression. Body / nav / card-brut / btn-ghost / textarea-brut / pipeline / marketing-page-bg all PASS spec exactly. CRITICAL: every spec line that depends on the violet accent (.btn-brut primary CTA bg, .btn-brut border, .textarea-brut:focus border-color, likely .suggest-chip hover, .conf-ribbon text) is broken because the CSS custom property `--accent` is declared twice in :root of /app/frontend/src/index.css. Line 19 sets `--accent: #7C5CFF` (the Bracket token), then line 46 redefines `--accent: 253 100% 68%` (shadcn HSL fragment). The second declaration wins so any rule of the form `background: var(--accent)` resolves to the literal string `253 100% 68%` which is INVALID CSS, and the property falls back to its initial value (transparent for background, currentColor for border). Visible end-user impact: landing 'Start a project' CTA and dashboard 'New project' CTA render as text-only — no violet pill. Spec calls for rgb(124,92,255).

ui_bugs.issue: Computed background = rgba(0,0,0,0) instead of rgb(124,92,255). Visible on landing 'Start a project →' and dashboard 'New project' button — they render as plain text, no violet pill, no border. Root cause: `--accent` CSS variable redefined as HSL fragment '253 100% 68%' in the shadcn :root block (line 46) shadowing the hex value '#7C5CFF' from the Bracket token block (line 19). Disabled state still works because it uses `--surface-3` / `--text-3` which are not shadowed.

On focus the border-color resolves to rgb(243,244,246) (white text token) instead of the spec rgb(124,92,255) violet. Same root cause — rule is `border-color: var(--accent)` which is now invalid. The 3px outer box-shadow IS rgba(124,92,255,0.18) because that rule uses a literal rgba(), so the violet glow is visible but the inner 1px ring is white.

Suggest chip below Step 1 'WHAT' textarea renders with bg=transparent, border=0px, radius=0px — none of the .suggest-chip styling is applying. Need to confirm whether the chip JSX still carries the class name or if the class definition itself fails due to the --accent variable bug.

Output card on Step 1 does NOT have a `.liquid-glass` class in the DOM (querySelector('.liquid-glass') returned null). The card still renders dark-surfaced and visually OK (looks like it's rendered with default surface/border tokens) but the spec-named class is absent. May indicate the rewrite removed .liquid-glass from JSX or replaced the class — confirm the JSX class wiring on the output card.

integration_issues.issue: One non-blocking console error fires after typing in Step 1 WHAT textarea: 'Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 400'. Did not investigate which endpoint — likely the suggest or autosave endpoint when payload is incomplete.

action_items: FIX --accent variable collision in /app/frontend/src/index.css. Two options: (a) Keep the Bracket hex '#7C5CFF' value and rename the shadcn HSL fragment to a separate name like `--shadcn-accent: 253 100% 68%;` plus update any `hsl(var(--accent))` shadcn references in tailwind.config or component CSS to `hsl(var(--shadcn-accent))`. (b) Alternatively keep --accent in HSL fragment form and rewrite all Bracket rules from `background: var(--accent)` to `background: hsl(var(--accent))` — but option (a) is safer and lower-blast-radius. After fix verify: .btn-brut computed bg = rgb(124, 92, 255), .textarea-brut:focus border-color = rgb(124, 92, 255).

Confirm .liquid-glass class is still on the Step 1 OutputCard JSX (testid step1-framing-output). querySelector('.liquid-glass') returned null on /project/:id/flow — either the class was dropped or the card is wrapped in a different class.
Investigate the 400 error fired on Step 1 textarea input — likely an autosave/suggest endpoint failing for partial payloads. Non-blocking but noisy in console.
critical_code_review_comments: Two :root blocks defining the same custom property (`--accent`) with different value formats is a maintenance footgun — any future contributor will hit this trap. Recommend isolating shadcn HSL fragments behind a `--sc-` namespace (e.g. `--sc-primary`, `--sc-accent`) to fully decouple from the Bracket design tokens.

Mixed value formats (hex `#7C5CFF` for Bracket tokens, HSL fragments for shadcn) means `var(--x)` is not interchangeable — every usage must be audited. Consider linting custom property naming for sanity.

index.css is 475 lines and growing — fine for now but the legacy alias bloat (`.btn-brut`, `.card-brut`, `.liquid-glass`, `.clay`, `.clay-signal`, `.story-rail`, etc.) suggests the next refactor should delete legacy class names from JSX in favor of the new Linear-named utilities, not just remap them in CSS.

success_rate.frontend: 70% — 7 of 10 visual-regression checks pass; 3 fail (all caused by one root cause: --accent variable shadowing)

Everything else in iteration_16 already passes — Body bg/color/font, nav .glass, .card-brut, .btn-ghost, .textarea-brut idle, .step-pipeline active styles, marketing pages, disabled CTAs, Step nav 1..5 — all confirmed Linear-spec compliant.
rca of the issue: ROOT CAUSE: /app/frontend/src/index.css lines 9-31 declare the Bracket design tokens including `--accent: #7C5CFF`. Lines 33-50 declare the shadcn semantic vars in HSL-fragment format (intended to be used as `hsl(var(--accent))` ), redeclaring `--accent: 253 100% 68%`. Both blocks are inside :root, so the second declaration wins per CSS cascade. As a result, every rule of form `background: var(--accent)` or `border-color: var(--accent)` resolves to the invalid value `253 100% 68%` and falls back to the property's initial value (transparent / currentColor). REPRODUCTION: `getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--accent')` returns '253 100% 68%' instead of '#7C5CFF'. FIX: rename one of the two `--accent` declarations. Lowest-blast-radius patch is to namespace the shadcn HSL fragments (e.g. prefix with `--sc-`) and update any tailwind.config or shadcn component CSS that consumes them via `hsl(var(--accent))`. After fix, .btn-brut, .btn-brut:hover (var(--accent-2) is unaffected, already hex), .textarea-brut:focus, .suggest-chip:hover, .conf-ribbon text-color and any other accent-driven rules will render violet as specified.
